<p>*Release date: 2017-03-24* High-speed steel is an extremely important cutting tool material, accounting for 45% of the world's cutting tool sales, among which accounting for 85% of the sales of complex multi-edged cutting tools such as gear cutting tools and broaches. It gathers excellent red hardness, wear resistance, impact resistance and heat treatability together, can be processed into shape in the soft annealing state, and then through quenching, tempering heat treatment to precipitate a large amount of secondary carbides, to achieve the hardening and strengthening of the material, has obvious advantages that cemented carbide and cermet tools do not have. According to the preparation method, high-speed steel can be divided into traditional cast and forged high-speed steel and powder metallurgy high-speed steel. Due to the higher alloy elements and carbon element content of high-speed steel, casting high-speed steel has unavoidable disadvantages such as coarse structure, compositional segregation and property anisotropy. The emergence of powder metallurgy high-speed steel fundamentally avoids the appearance of coarse carbides, has the advantages of fine and uniform carbide structure, property isotropy, etc., is a milestone in the development history of high-speed steel. However, our country does not have the production capacity of high-performance powder metallurgy high-speed steel. Commercial powder metallurgy high-speed steel appeared in the 1970s, mainly including gas atomization-heat isostatic pressing method, spray deposition method and super solid-phase liquid-phase sintering method. The gas atomization-heat isostatic pressing process uses gas atomization method to prepare high-speed steel powder, and then obtains densified steel ingots through heat isostatic pressing, which can prepare fully dense, fine and uniform structure, stable quality, excellent performance and large-size workpieces, but has the disadvantages of expensive equipment, high technical threshold, large pollution and high energy consumption. Spray forming process is a low-cost method for preparing high-speed steel, has the advantages of short process, low cost and high production efficiency, but also has the disadvantages of high energy consumption, large pollution, alloying limitation, relatively high impurity content and non-dense core. The super solid-phase liquid-phase sintering process is a sintering temperature in the liquid phase + austenite + carbide phase region, achieves densification with the help of the appearance of a part of liquid phase, has the advantages of short process, small investment, low cost, high material utilization rate, suitable for small-scale production, can prepare nitrogen-containing high-speed steel, but the liquid phase promotes rod-like or coarse carbides to distribute along grain boundaries, is the worst structure among these three preparation methods. The emergence of Sharpen New Materials non-atomized powder ball milling method for preparing powder high-speed steel brought encouraging news to the domestication of high-performance powder high-speed steel. The non-atomized powder ball milling method creatively uses non-atomized ball milled mixed powder as raw material, can add the required alloy elements almost without limitation, through solid-phase vacuum activation sintering method, one step to achieve the preparation of near-net-shape billet, and then through heat treatment.</p>
